context.description: Naracoorte is a Limestone Coast town on the road between Adelaide and Melbourne. South of town, Naracoorte Caves National Park is South Australia's only World Heritage site, with caves that preserved the bones of Australian megafauna over the last two to three million years. To the south the terra rossa soil of Coonawarra and Penola grows Cabernet Sauvignon, while Bool Lagoon to the south-west is a large wetland for waterbirds. The town's flour-mill museum covers the wool industry.

context.description: Murray Bridge is a city of about 17,500 on the River Murray, 76 km south-east of Adelaide, named for the road bridge opened here in 1879. The river brings houseboats, wakeboarding, fishing and walks along its banks and wetlands. Monarto Safari Park, on the plains west of town, keeps lions, giraffes, rhinos and elephants. Low rainfall and little light pollution on the outskirts also make it good for stargazing.

context.description: Mannum sits on the Murray River just over an hour from Adelaide. It is known as the birthplace of the Murray paddle steamers, and the dock museum and Mary Ann Reserve tell that story. Riverbank pubs overlook the water, and kayakers head downstream to a bird sanctuary lined with river red gums. Mannum Waterfalls and the Palmer granite outcrops sit a short drive inland.

context.description: Coorong National Park runs along a chain of salty lagoons behind the Younghusband Peninsula, about 200 km south-east of Adelaide. The wetland is of international importance and is known for pelicans and migratory waders. Visitors bird-watch, walk, fish, kayak, camp and drive 4WD tracks, and Ngarrindjeri and European history runs through the park. Access is via Meningie or Kingston off the Princes Highway.
